title: ProofResult
description: The machine output a warrant is granted against.

command.description: The exact command that produced it, so VDS S-7(2)(1) is checkable.

digest.description: The digest a warrant cites. Covers the run's FINDINGS and inputs, and deliberately not its timing, so an unchanged input re-run cites the same evidence (VDS S-7(2)(1)).

notes.description: Lines the run printed that are not violations: reliance on a reserved clause, a deprecated consumer, a carve-out that was taken.

rows_skipped_reasons.description: Count per reason a row was considered but not enforced, so a vacuous pass is diagnosable rather than merely flagged.

warrant_id.description: Set when a warrant cites this record. Null until then.

surface_digest.description: The digest of exactly what was accepted, so a later claim that a screen was accepted is checkable against the bytes (VDS S-6(7)).

role.description: ARIA role, or null where the component is a layout container with none.

CaptureMode.description: VDS S-7(2)(5): a hand-written proof record is void, and the contract enforces it by admitting exactly one value.

importPath.description: The module specifier a screen imports from, as written in the import.

ComponentId.description: A registered component, allocated as the highest on disk plus one (VDS S-4(4)).

ContrastFloor.description:
A contrast floor: a REQUIREMENT, never a realisation (VDS S-2(6)).

`boundary` and `against` name tokens or edges BY NAME. A literal value in either is a storing-form violation of VDS S-2(2), and `no_stored_values` looks for exactly that.

basis.description: Where the requirement comes from, e.g. "WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11".

Demand.description: How many routes consume this component. Measured, never estimated (VDS S-5(7)), which is why the command that measured it is part of the value.

measuredBy.description: The exact command that produced the count.

EvidenceEntry.description:
One proof a warrant rests on.

`digest` is copied from the record on disk and never from a caller: a warrant that cites a digest the caller supplied proves the caller.

nodeId.description: A Figma node id, which is `<digits>:<digits>` in a file URL and `<digits>-<digits>` in a deep link. Both spellings are accepted because both are what a designer actually copies.

FloorScope.description:
What kind of thing the boundary is.

VDS S-9(5): where a lower floor is genuinely correct, the lawful move is to change the component's SCOPE and state the basis, not to loosen the ratio. A factual claim about scope is contestable by a reviewer; a quietly lowered floor is not. That is why this field exists at all.

InvokedBy.description: What invoked the run. VDS S-7(2)(3) requires something other than the author choosing to run it, and VDS S-7(3) holds that a hook is not CI.

oneOf.description:
The HTML `<label>` association: a `for`/`id` pair, or a control wrapped by its label element.

Added because the set without it could not describe a text input, which is the single most common named control there is. `aria_labelledby` is a DIFFERENT mechanism, not a spelling of this one: it points at arbitrary elements by id and overrides the label association, so recording one where the code does the other publishes a contract the code does not keep. Found by adopting VDS on `examples/storefront`, where the only honest value for TextField was absent from the enum.

ProofId.description: A captured proof result, stamped with the UTC second it was captured.

ProofKind.description: The closed registry at VDS S-7(5).

oneOf.description: Every component referenced by any declared screen exists in the register.
The register agrees with the codebase and with Figma, both directions.
No screen uses an unregistered component. The anti-drift proof.
Every registered component's boundaries clear their floors in every theme.
Every required state of every registered component is drawn.
Each registered component's code counterpart matches its contract.
The two named records agree where the pin declares them aligned.
A component proposed for retirement has zero remaining consumers.
Each generated ledger is current with its source.

ProofStatus.description:
The three outcomes a proof record may carry.

There is no "skipped" and no "warning". VDS S-7(2)(4) requires a pass over zero enforceable rows to be recorded as `vacuous` and never as `passed`, and the absence of a fourth variant is what makes that structural.

figmaProperty.description: The corresponding Figma variant property, or null where the prop has no visual counterpart.

type.description:
The TypeScript type expression, or a closed union written `a|b|c`.

Serialised as `type`, which is the field name the contract publishes and a reserved word in Rust. The rename keeps the published shape rather than letting an implementation-language constraint leak into the artefact.

State.description: The nine states, fixed by VDS S-5(3). A record may require a subset. It may not invent a tenth, and here it cannot.

StateContract.description:
Which of the nine states are required, which are drawn, which are built.

Stored as sorted, deduplicated vectors rather than sets so the serialised form is stable: a record's bytes must not depend on hash iteration order, or the register digest moves without the register moving.

Status.description: The lifecycle at VDS S-5(4). A directed path where skipping is forbidden.

Surface.description:
The surface a warrant was granted over. VDS S-6(4): a change to either digest spends the warrant.

Both digests are computed from LIVE state, never read back from a generated artefact. A surface digest taken from a ledger would go stale exactly when a screen changed and the ledger was not regenerated, which is the one moment it has to be right.

Timestamp.description: UTC, second resolution, trailing Z. The one canonical form VDS writes.

Violation.description: One finding. `expected` and `actual` are both required and both non-empty, because a finding that says only what is wrong makes the reader guess at what right would have been.

location.description: `file:line`, or a route plus a component id.

rule.description: The invariant id or statute section the violation offends.

WarrantId.description: A warrant record. The stage number is part of the identifier so the four series are independent.

oneOf.description: The surface it was granted over changed (VDS S-6(4)). Recorded, never deleted.
